quick_stats.best_time: Mar (spring equinox festival); Oct – Apr (dry, pleasant)

quick_warnings: Bernal is a tiny Pueblo Mágico — it gets very crowded on weekends and holidays; visit midweek for a calmer experience.
The Peña hike is exposed and steep toward the top; bring water, sunscreen, and start early in the morning.
Few ATMs in town and some shops are cash-only — bring pesos from Querétaro.

detail_guide.getting_around: Bernal is a small village easily explored on foot in an hour. From Querétaro city, it is a 40-minute drive or colectivo ride. There is no public transit within Bernal itself. Parking can be scarce on weekends; arrive early.

top_sights.name: Peña de Bernal
top_sights.description: A 350-meter monolith — the world's third tallest — with a well-marked hiking trail to a viewpoint about two-thirds up.

top_sights.name: Centro Histórico de Bernal
top_sights.description: Charming cobblestone streets with colorful buildings, artisan shops selling wool textiles, and the Parroquia de San Sebastián.

parks.name: Sendero de la Peña
parks.description: The main trail ascending the Peña, passing through scrubland with cactus and wildflowers and ending at a dramatic viewpoint.

eat_drink_work.name: Gorditas de Bernal
eat_drink_work.description: Bernal is famous for its gorditas de migaja (pork-crackle stuffed corn cakes) sold from stalls around the main plaza.

eat_drink_work.description: Nearby sparkling wine estate offering cave tours, tastings, and vineyard views in the Querétaro wine country.

eat_drink_work.name: Café de la Peña
